title: Zorb Learns How $730 of Pizza Became $3,155.02
description:
Zorb skips pizza for a year and discovers compound interest: money that earns interest on its own interest. The pizza and $100 examples come from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's Investor.gov lesson on compound interest.

Education, not financial advice.

#Shorts #compoundinterest #personalfinance

beats.line: Stop. Your 730 dollars of skipped pizza becomes 3,155.02 dollars. How?
Skip a 2 dollar slice every day for a year. That is 730 dollars.
Lock it somewhere that pays 5 percent a year. Then wait.
The trick: 100 dollars at 5 percent becomes 105. Next year, 110.25.
That extra quarter is interest on interest. Money making baby money.
After 30 years, the pizza money is 3,155.02 dollars.
Earthlings call this compound interest. Zorb calls it pizza that never stops growing.
Zorb will return. Earth money remains confusing.
